title: Keloid scar treatment
what: A keloid is a firm, raised scar that grows beyond the edge of the wound. It is made softer and flatter with injections, pressure dressings, and other methods.
why: When a scar grows, itches, hurts, or bothers you.
duration: one visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; treatment usually lasts several months
tell_doctor: When and after what the scar appeared
If you or relatives had keloids before
What treatment you have already tried

prepare.title: Photos
prepare.text: Take a photo of the scar before treatment. This makes it easier to judge the result.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Clothes that make the scar easy to uncover.

steps: The doctor examines the scar and chooses a method
The skin is cleaned with antiseptic
Often medicine is injected into the scar with a thin needle
Sometimes silicone patches or pressure dressings are prescribed
The next visit is booked, usually after a few weeks
feel: Injections into the scar can be felt, because the tissue is firm
After the injection, the spot may ache for a day or two
after: Use the patches or dressings as your doctor said
Protect the scar from the sun
Come for repeat treatments on schedule
red_flags: The scar becomes inflamed, has pus, or is surrounded by strong redness

faq.q: Can a keloid just be cut out?
faq.a: Without extra treatment, it often grows back, sometimes bigger. That is why the doctor combines methods.
Usually several, a few weeks apart. Your doctor will say after the exam.

reminders.text: Scar treatment tomorrow. Bring reports from past treatment, if you had any.
